conservation.condition_narrative: The support is in good condition, despite having a convex curvature with slight attendant creases. More prominent creases are visible at the lower left and right corners, as well as the upper left corner. All four corners are discolored at the tips. There is a gouge on the left side next to a blue paint transfer. At the lower right of the design, the medium is smudged. A reddish discoloration is visible at the upper right. There are two stains, possibly ink, in the upper right quadrant. Surface accretions are scattered throughout.
conservation.technical_description:
**Support:** The support is a smooth, sized off-white paper. 
 
 
 
**Ground or Support Preparation:** Other than the sizing, there is no additional support preparation. 
 
 
 
**Design Layers:** The design layer consists of graphite, applied with varying pressure to complete the design. 
 
 
 
**Surface Coating:** There is no surface coating. 
 
 
 
**Framing, Backing, and Hanging Hardware:** The painting is installed in a whitewashed maple frame, with a secondary basswood backing strainer. The entire framing package consists of a micro-environmentally controlled package containing the artwork, with a micro-chamber board sealed with Marvelseal. This package rests on a foam core base that is over the strainer. The frame holds the Optium glazing in front of the artwork. Attached to the strainer are mirror hangers and "T" bolt security hardware for use during exhibition. The artwork is hinged to a drop-back, window backing mat with mulberry fiber paper hinges passed to the verso of the drop-back and secured with wheat starch paste and a mulberry paper T. The drop-back is secured to the surrounding backing mat with acid-free paper tape. The window mat is hinged to the backing mat, and the entire package is backed with a micro-chamber corrugated board and sealed to the Optium glazing using Marvelseal and J-Lar tape.

description: Graphite sketch of an open tent door at night. The sketch consists of a large, slightly tilted, triangular shape. The top of the triangular shape extends almost to the top of the paper. A faint line, designating the pole used to hold the tent up, runs from the top of the triangle to the base.
